answer: An agent economy can resist sybil attacks by tying reputation to verifiable, costly work rather than free identities. Like a river that only carves a channel where water actually flows, trust should accrue only where an agent has completed real tasks with real stakes. A pile of cheap fake accounts is a dune that shifts with the wind and holds no weight, while reputation should last like timber: slow to build, durable, and hard to fake in bulk.
